newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Housing Bank to double its capital.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Housing Bank to double its capital.

text.p: Shareholders of Jordan's Housing Bank have approved a doubling of its capital to 50 million dinars ($70.6 million) to help expand its financing role, bank officials said on Saturday.

The bank's shareholders approved at an extraordinary AGM meeting on Friday a recommendation by the board to raise its capital by a private placement from existing shareholders along with subscriptions from local and foreign investors.
Officials, who say Gulf investors have shown interest in participating in a new issue, do not expect a final decision on the shape of the capital hike before June, bank officials said.
The bank has also not ruled out a GDR (Global Depository Receipt) issue, although that option appears less likely, they said.

The capital increase will help raise the bank's competitiveness and its financing role both in the local market and regionally after a new law passed last month widened its scope of operations to comprehensive banking.

A newly elected 13-member board of the bank, which includes representatives from state shareholders Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, and Iran, reappointed Jordanian banker Zuhair Khoury as chairman and executive president of the bank.
Abdul-Qader Dweik, formerly deputy general manager, was elected as general manager.

Bank officials say Housing Bank's strategic focus is to expand into comprehensive banking and away from its original real estate credit niche along with widening its investment and private banking business for its clients in capital markets.
Housing Bank's total assets stood at 1.136 billion dinars by the end of 1996 and its deposits stood at 918 million dinars.

The bank, which is Jordan's second largest bank, has Arab and foreign investors including Kuwait with a 20 percent stake and equal 6 percent stakes by Oman, Qatar and Iran. Jordan's government owns 18 percent.
